title: Write and revise in chat
summary: Use a conversation to turn rough notes into a message. Ask for a second draft in the same chat.

intro.what: Draft and revise one message without losing the thread.
intro.features: A chat keeps the turns together so you can ask for a shorter draft.
intro.exchange: Use a fictional mail handoff to test this surface.
intro.m365: Apply the same check to an approved practice note.
intro.developer: Try the example with a small local project.

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: A chat keeps the turns together so you can ask for a shorter draft.

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Open Claude and start a new chat. Paste the note below and its question together.
Mail queued at 09:00. One test arrived at 09:12. Other routes have not been tested.
Write two sentences for a handoff. Separate the one test that passed from the routes we still need to check.
Check your result. The update names the successful test and leaves other routes open.
In that same chat send “Shorten this to one sentence. Keep the successful test and the untested routes.” Check for both facts again.

sections.title: What it cannot do
paragraphs: A draft alone cannot tell you whether a mail repair worked. Supply a test result before asking for a verdict.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: The free plan has a session allowance. The number of messages can vary with demand.

sections.title: Gotchas
paragraphs: Watch for a draft that turns one successful test into a claim about the whole service.

sections.title: Official docs
paragraphs: Open the first guide for the controls. Use the second to check access or compare the related feature.

intro.features: Project knowledge holds reference material. Project instructions tell Claude how to use it.
intro.exchange: Trace a delivery claim back to the sample report.
intro.m365: Find the exact line in a practice policy.
intro.developer: Keep the input files beside your test results.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: Project knowledge holds reference material. Project instructions tell Claude how to use it.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Open Projects. Create Practice desk. Save the entire practice handbook below in a text file. On the project page use + to add that file. Start a chat in the project.
Practice handbook, revision B: only closed requests go in the weekly count. The sample has two closed and one open.
Add the handbook to a practice project. In a fresh project chat ask for the weekly count and the rule used.
Check your result. The answer gives two closed requests and points to revision B.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: What it cannot do
paragraphs: A file left on your desk is outside the project knowledge you supplied. Add the right version before asking about a change.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Free accounts can create up to five projects. Paid plans can use retrieval when the project knowledge grows large.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

sections.title: Gotchas
paragraphs: A rule left in an unrelated chat can be missing here. Ask which revision supports the answer.
sources: How can I create and manage projects?

paragraphs: Open the first guide for the controls. Use the second to check access or compare the related feature.

title: Build a small tool in Artifacts

intro.what: Make a small working counter you can try beside the chat.
intro.features: An Artifact opens the generated work in its own pane. Ask for a change and test the preview again.
intro.exchange: Test a pretend queue counter with zero messages.
intro.m365: Try two rows from a fictional request list.
intro.developer: Run the smallest working screen before adding another feature.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: An Artifact opens the generated work in its own pane. Ask for a change and test the preview again.
sources: What are artifacts and how do I use them?

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Start a Claude chat. Ask for the counter below as an interactive Artifact. Open its preview.
The tally starts at zero. Count adds one. Reset returns to zero.
Make an interactive tally artifact with Count and Reset. Show the score as a number.
Check your result. Two Count clicks show 2. Reset shows 0.

sections.title: What it cannot do
paragraphs: A working preview cannot prove that a published copy stores data or works offline. Test those promises separately.

paragraphs: Artifacts are offered on free and paid plans. Persistent storage on web and desktop is a paid-plan feature.

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: Claude Code can read project files, propose edits and run checks in the working folder.
sources: Models, usage, and limits in Claude Code

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Make a practice folder with an index.html containing <button>Clear All</button>. Open that folder in Claude Code. Give it the task below.
A practice counter page shows the right number but calls its reset button Clear All.
In the practice folder, find the reset button. Rename its label to Reset. Show the changed lines and the result of one reset test.
Check your result. Only the label changes. A score of 2 still resets to 0.

intro.features: Connectors let Claude use information or tools from another service with the access you grant.
intro.exchange: Use a fictional mail handoff to test this surface.

sources: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: Connectors let Claude use information or tools from another service with the access you grant.
sources: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: In an approved practice Drive folder, create a document named Shift card. Put only “Window B” on line one. In Claude choose Customize, Connectors, then +. Choose the approved service and Connect. Sign in with the practice account.
An approved training folder contains a note called Shift card. Its first line reads Window B.
Using only the approved connector, find Shift card. Quote its first line. Say unknown if you cannot open it. Make no changes.
Check your result. The reply says Window B and identifies the note, or explains it could not read it.
sources: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

paragraphs: Connecting a service does not grant every member access to everything in it. Use a practice item the signed-in account can open.

paragraphs: Web connectors are available across plans. In Team and Enterprise, an owner must first enable connectors for members.

title: Rehearse a handoff aloud
summary: Talk through a problem and hear the answer. Switch back to text to check details such as times or file names.

intro.what: Practice speaking a short handoff and check what was heard.
intro.features: Voice mode lets you talk and hear the reply. You can inspect the resulting chat.
intro.exchange: Use a fictional mail handoff to test this surface.
intro.m365: Apply the same check to an approved practice note.
intro.developer: Try the example with a small local project.

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: Voice mode lets you talk and hear the reply. You can inspect the resulting chat.

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Open a fresh Claude chat. Choose the voice control and allow the microphone. Say the two counts below, then stop and read the transcript.
The queue held fifteen items before lunch and five after lunch.
Read those counts aloud. Ask for a one-sentence handoff and a separate line with the two numbers.
Check your result. The written numbers are 15 and 5, in that order.

sections.title: What it cannot do
paragraphs: Speech can be misheard. A spoken summary cannot settle whether you said fifteen or fifty. Read back the saved text.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Voice sessions use the regular allowance for the account. Push-to-talk gives you control of the microphone in a noisy room.

sections.title: Gotchas
paragraphs: Fifteen and fifty can sound alike. Check the transcript before accepting the total.

sections.title: Official docs
paragraphs: Open the first guide for the controls. Use the second to check access or compare the related feature.

title: Read a file or inspect an image
summary: Attach a supported document or image and ask a question tied to one visible detail. Use a small file first.

intro.what: Ask about a page or image you can compare by eye.
intro.features: A chat attachment supplies a particular file. Project knowledge can supply the same material again later.
intro.exchange: Trace a delivery claim back to the sample report.
intro.m365: Find the exact line in a practice policy.
intro.developer: Keep the input files beside your test results.

sections.title: What it is for
paragraphs: A chat attachment supplies a particular file. Project knowledge can supply the same material again later.

sections.title: Do this first
paragraphs: Create a one-page practice file with the counts below. Choose Add files or photos in a new chat, attach the file and ask the question.
A short practice PDF has a table showing 2 requests open and 3 closed.
Attach the practice page. Name both row labels, give their values and calculate the total. Flag any cell you cannot read.
Check your result. The rows say open 2 and closed 3. The total is 5.

sections.title: What it cannot do
paragraphs: A blurry screenshot cannot establish what a missing digit says. Ask for unknown rather than filling it in.

sections.title: Plan and availability
paragraphs: Chat and project uploads have different limits. The upload guide lists 20 files per chat and a smaller per-file size for project knowledge.

sections.title: Gotchas
paragraphs: If the table is scanned or cropped, read the column labels yourself. Ask which cells were visible.

sections.title: Official docs
paragraphs: Open the first guide for the controls. Use the second to check access or compare the related feature.
